paramecium.about: Paramecium (also Paramoecium) is a genus of unicellular ciliates, commonly studied as a representative of the ciliate group. Paramecia are widespread in freshwater, brackish, and marine environments and are often very abundant in stagnant basins and ponds.

euglena.about: Euglena is a genus of single-celled flagellate eukaryotes. It is the best known and most widely studied member of the class Euglenoidea, a diverse group containing some 54 genera and at least 800 species. Species of Euglena are found in fresh and salt waters.

amoeba.about: Amoeba, alternatively Chaos diffluens, is an amoeba closely related to the giant amoebae and a species commonly bought at science supply stores.

rotifer.about: The rotifers (Rotifera, commonly called wheel animals) make up a phylum of microscopic and near-microscopic pseudocoelomate animals.

volvox.about: Volvox is a polyphyletic genus of chlorophyte green algae in the family Volvocaceae. It forms spherical colonies of up to 50,000 cells. They live in a variety of freshwater habitats, and were first reported by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek in 1700.

diatom.about: Diatoms are a major group of microalgae, and are among the most common types of phytoplankton.

daphnia.about: Daphnia, a genus of small planktonic crustaceans, are 0.2–5 millimetres (0.01–0.20 in) in length.

tardigrade.about: Tardigrades are water-dwelling, eight-legged, segmented micro-animals. They were first discovered by the German zoologist Johann August Ephraim Goeze in 1773.

doubles.about: Two golden giants in the lion's mane.

doubles.name: COR CAROLI (ALPHA CANUM VENATICORUM)
doubles.about: Charles's Heart, under the handle of the Plough.

doubles.name: GRAFFIAS (BETA SCORPII)
doubles.about: Blue-white pair at the scorpion's claws.

doubles.name: RIGEL (BETA ORIONIS)
doubles.about: A faint companion almost lost in the glare of Orion's foot.

doubles.name: POLARIS (ALPHA URSAE MINORIS)
doubles.about: The pole star has a small companion, a test for a small telescope.

doubles.name: GAMMA DELPHINI
doubles.about: The dolphin's nose: yellow and, to some eyes, green.

doubles.name: ACHIRD (ETA CASSIOPEIAE)
doubles.about: A sun like ours with a small red companion.

doubles.name: 61 CYGNI
doubles.about: Two orange dwarfs 11 light-years off: the first star whose distance was measured, in 1838.

doubles.name: IOTA CANCRI
doubles.about: The winter Albireo: yellow and blue.

doubles.name: BETA MONOCEROTIS
doubles.about: Herschel called it one of the most beautiful sights in the heavens; the companion is double too.

doubles.name: PORRIMA (GAMMA VIRGINIS)
doubles.about: Twin stars 169 years round each other, opening again since their close pass in 2005.

doubles.name: RASALGETHI (ALPHA HERCULIS)
doubles.about: A red supergiant with a companion that looks green beside it.

doubles.name: ALNITAK (ZETA ORIONIS)
doubles.about: The east star of Orion's belt, a tight pair.

moon.name: MARE IMBRIUM
moon.about: The Sea of Showers: a basin 1,100 km wide, flooded with lava 3.5 billion years ago.

moon.name: MARE SERENITATIS
moon.about: The Sea of Serenity. Apollo 17 landed on its eastern shore.

moon.name: MARE TRANQUILLITATIS
moon.about: The Sea of Tranquillity, where people first walked on the Moon.

moon.name: MARE CRISIUM
moon.about: The Sea of Crises, an oval sea on its own near the edge.

moon.name: MARE NECTARIS
moon.about: The Sea of Nectar, a small round sea.

moon.name: OCEANUS PROCELLARUM
moon.about: The Ocean of Storms, the largest of the dark plains.

moon.name: MARE FRIGORIS
moon.about: The Sea of Cold, a long strip across the north.

moon.name: TYCHO
moon.about: A young crater 85 km wide; its bright rays cross the whole face at full Moon.

moon.name: COPERNICUS
moon.about: A terraced crater 93 km wide, 800 million years old.

moon.name: KEPLER
moon.about: A small bright crater with rays.

moon.name: ARISTARCHUS
moon.about: The brightest spot on the Moon.

moon.name: PLATO
moon.about: A dark, flat-floored crater 100 km wide on the shore of Mare Imbrium.

moon.name: CLAVIUS
moon.about: One of the largest craters, 230 km wide, with a curve of smaller ones inside.

moon.name: APOLLO 11
moon.about: Tranquility Base: Armstrong and Aldrin landed here on 20 July 1969.
